simple.meaning: נָכַל (nâkal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to defraud , i.e. act treacherously.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Genesis, Numbers, Psalms, Malachi, beginning at Genesis 37:18. Its contexts include family, family line, flock, sacrifice, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָכַל (H5230).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָכַל (nâkal) / H5230 is traced through Genesis 37:18, Numbers 25:18, Psalms 105:25, Malachi 1:14 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5230. nakal [ נָכַל ] verb be crafty, deceitful, knavish (Assyrian nakâlu, be crafty, cunning; נְכֵל ᵑ7 be crafty , Pa`el deceive ; Syriac deceive, plot ; compare perhaps act faithlessly , faithless , Prä Amhar. Spr. 90 ); — Qal Participle נוֺכֵל Mal 1:14 knave . Pi`el Perfect 3masculine plural with accusative of congnate meaning with verb לָכֶם נִכְּלוּ אֲשֶׁר נִכְלֵיהֶם Num 25:18 their wiles with which they beguiled you . Hithpa`el Imperfect לַהֲמִיתוֺ אֹתוֺ וַיִּתְנַכְּלוּ Gen 37:18 they knavishly planned against him (Kö iii. 9 ), etc.; Infinitive construct בְ לְחִתְנַכֵּל Psa 105:25 to deal knavishly with .
